independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived from the bytes rather than the row. Span WEB 52:1-5 = MT 52:3-7; Psalm 52 is a +2 psalm whose title occupies MT 52:1-2, and every dual-cite in the row satisfies that arithmetic, including both title verses. Both Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier against the refs they are cited to: “אָהַ֣בְתָּ רָּ֣ע” at oshb:Ps.52.5 (the dagesh in the resh of רָּ֣ע is source-true, not a typo) and the same verb alone. The repetition claim holds without overreach: MT 52:6 opens אָהַ֥בְתָּ against MT 52:5's אָהַ֣בְתָּ, which collate returns at accent_stripped tier (the accent differs, the consonants and pointing do not), and the row asserts only that the verb repeats, never byte identity, so the tier is adequate to the claim. Selah is handled correctly in both direction and weight: the inventory carries selah at MT 52:5 and MT 52:7, one occurrence each, and both are verse-final in both witnesses — WEB 52:3 ends “You love evil more than good, lying rather than speaking the truth. Selah.” (web:Ps.52.3) and WEB 52:5 ends “and root you out of the land of the living. Selah.” (web:Ps.52.5) — so ‘after 52:3 and after 52:5’ is exact, and the row caps both as interior/end corroboration behind the second-person-address driver. The back seam is the real signal and it is byte-visible: 2ms address runs unbroken through MT 52:3-7, then MT 52:8 opens “וְיִרְא֖וּ צַדִּיקִ֥ים”, third plural. No selah, K/Q, or seg-layer claim is made that the inventories contradict; Psalm 52's K/Q inventory is empty. Confidence high is calibrated. One observation, not contested: device_notes' ‘this +2 psalm's rows dual-cite both MT title verses throughout’ is an unswept universal and reads as row-set bookkeeping rather than text evidence; under the narrow reading (wherever the title is cited, both MT verses are) it is true of this psalm's rows, so I do not file it.

Span WEB 52:6-9 = MT 52:8-11, arithmetic verified per verse. The Hebrew quote “וְיִרְא֖וּ צַדִּיקִ֥ים” collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Ps.52.8 and the gloss is right in the one place this verse can trap a reader: MT 52:8 pairs וְיִרְא֖וּ (from ‘see’) with the near-homophone וְיִירָ֗אוּ (from ‘fear’), and the row's rendering keeps them distinct. The addressee shift the row rests on is real and is the strongest available warrant at this seam. Selah at MT 52:7 is correctly cited as front-seam corroboration and explicitly denied driver status, which is the right weight. Out-of-span material (52:1-5) is mirrored in the refs array. What fails is the second stated ground of the rejected_alternative: it denies any speech-frame marker at exactly the point where WEB closes the righteous' reported speech and MT opens a contrastive independent pronoun. The span itself stands — the row's first ground (shared vantage against the wicked man) carries it, and medium confidence is appropriately calibrated — but the rejected_alternative's stated evidence is false as written.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative rejects a 52:6-7 | 52:8-9 split on the ground that ‘no further speech-frame marker separates them’, but the reported speech introduced at WEB 52:6 is closed at the end of WEB 52:7 and MT 52:10 opens with a contrastive independent pronoun — a speech-frame terminus plus voice pivot at precisely the considered split point.
challenges.evidence: WEB 52:6 introduces the speech: “The righteous also will see it, and fear, and laugh at him, saying,” (web:Ps.52.6). WEB 52:7 carries the quotation and closes it: ““Behold, this is the man who didn’t make God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness.”” (web:Ps.52.7) — the closing quotation mark is the frame terminus. WEB 52:8 then opens “But as for me, I am like a green olive tree” (web:Ps.52.8). MT confirms the pivot independently of the translator's punctuation: oshb:Ps.52.10 (= web:Ps.52.8) opens “וַאֲנִ֤י”, waw + independent 1cs pronoun, byte-spliced from verse_map_oshb; full verse: “וַאֲנִ֤י כְּזַ֣יִת רַ֭עֲנָן בְּבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּטַ֥חְתִּי בְחֶֽסֶד אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים עוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד”. So a frame marker does separate them; the ground as stated is not available. The span is not contested — the row's shared-vantage ground is sufficient.

reviews.reasoning: The structural call is sound and I do not contest it: six WEB verses (53:1-6 = MT 53:2-7), no vocative or speech-frame shift inside, title dual-cited correctly for a +1 psalm, and the inventory gives Psalm 53 no selah at all, consistent with the row making no selah claim. The row's one quantified claim re-derives exactly, and it is one of the few in this cluster that names its unit: sweeping the unsuffixed spelling of the divine name over MT 53:2-7 returns 7 occurrences across 5 verses (MT 53:2, 53:3, 53:5, 53:6, 53:7 — two each at 53:3 and 53:6, none at 53:4), and the unsuffixed Tetragrammaton spelling returns 0 occurrences / 0 verses in this psalm. The doublet relation with Psalm 14 is stated as a typed relation with no byte claim about the other psalm, which is in scope. Both Hebrew runs also collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs. The defects are lexical, and they are in the OL lane: at oshb:Ps.53.7 the row attaches the glosses ‘Zion’ and ‘Israel’ to two tokens that mean neither, each sitting exactly one token ahead of the word it names; and the 53:2 gloss covers a token the quoted span stops short of. Byte-true quotation with a false gloss is the failure mode this lens exists to catch, so the verdict is challenge despite the structure being right.

challenges.claim: At oshb:Ps.53.7 the row states that OSHB names יִתֵּ֣ן as ‘Zion’ and יְשֻׁע֪וֹת as ‘Israel’; both identifications are false — the verse's Zion and Israel are מִצִּיּוֹן֮ and יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל, while יִתֵּ֣ן is the verb ‘gives’ in the idiom מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן and יְשֻׁע֪וֹת is ‘salvation(s)’.
challenges.evidence: Byte-spliced MT 53:7 in full (verse_map_oshb, collate tier BYTE at oshb:Ps.53.7): “מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִּיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֪וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל”. Token order is מִ֥י / יִתֵּ֣ן / מִצִּיּוֹן֮ / יְשֻׁע֪וֹת / יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל, i.e. the row's two labels are each displaced one token to the left: the Zion token is מִצִּיּוֹן֮ (min + Zion) and the Israel token is יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל, not the two the row quotes. WEB 53:6 renders the same clause “Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!” (web:Ps.53.6), which maps salvation to יְשֻׁע֪וֹת and Zion to מִצִּיּוֹן֮, against the row. Dual-cite for the +1 psalm: web:Ps.53.6 = oshb:Ps.53.7. The quoted bytes are correct; only the identifications are wrong, so the cure is a re-gloss (or a re-cut onto the Zion and Israel tokens), not a re-quote.

challenges.claim: The Hebrew quote at oshb:Ps.53.2 ends at אֵ֣ין but its gloss reads ‘there-is-no God’, so the gloss covers a token that lies outside the quoted span.
challenges.evidence: The row quotes “אָ֘מַ֤ר נָבָ֣ל בְּ֭לִבּוֹ אֵ֣ין” (collate tier BYTE at oshb:Ps.53.2) and glosses it ‘said [the] fool in-his-heart, there-is-no God’. The divine name in that clause is the next token, אֱלֹהִ֑ים, which the quote does not reach; full MT 53:2 byte-spliced: “אָ֘מַ֤ר נָבָ֣ל בְּ֭לִבּוֹ אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים הִֽ֝שְׁחִ֗יתוּ וְהִֽתְעִ֥יבוּ עָ֝֗וֶל אֵ֣ין עֹֽשֵׂה טֽוֹב”. Quote and gloss must cover the same span, and the repair re-cuts one side or the other — extending the quote by one token to אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים keeps the gloss as written. Dual-cite: web:Ps.53.1 = oshb:Ps.53.2.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 54:1-7 = MT 54:3-9 with the title at MT 54:1-2; Psalm 54 is one of the four +2 psalms and the refs array carries both title verses with correct arithmetic. The whole-psalm call is policy-compliant at seven verses and I find no tier-1 rival seam strong enough to force a split. Selah verifies: the inventory has one occurrence at MT 54:5, it is verse-final in both witnesses — WEB 54:3 ends “They haven’t set God before them. Selah.” (web:Ps.54.3) — and the rejected_alternative explicitly caps it at tier-3 rather than leaning on it, which is the correct weight. All WEB quotes are verbatim. Two things I checked and cleared: Psalm 54 does carry a ketiv/qere at MT 54:7 (= web:Ps.54.5), but the row never quotes that verse, so no disclosure was owed; and the inline cite that attaches the Ziphites' words to oshb:Ps.54.1 sits one MT verse off the clause it quotes (the historical note is MT 54:2), which I do not file because the title pseudo-ref form is owner-ruled and the refs array carries both members. What I do file is the divine-name figure in device_notes: the numbers are right, but they ship with neither the swept object nor the unit, which is exactly the disclosure the count rules require and which this cluster's Psalm 53 row supplies correctly.

challenges.claim: The device_notes figure ‘4 Elohim / 1 YHWH this psalm’ names neither the swept object (the unsuffixed spellings, which is what these Elohistic-texture figures count) nor the unit (verses vs occurrences), and carries no sweep, although the figures themselves re-derive correctly.
challenges.evidence: Re-derived with the unit named, query spliced from source bytes: over MT 54:3-9 the unsuffixed spelling of Elohim returns 4 occurrences across 4 verses — oshb:Ps.54.3, oshb:Ps.54.4, oshb:Ps.54.5, oshb:Ps.54.6, one token each — and the unsuffixed Tetragrammaton spelling returns 1 occurrence across 1 verse, oshb:Ps.54.8 (“בִּנְדָבָ֥ה אֶזְבְּחָה לָּ֑ךְ א֤וֹדֶה שִּׁמְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה כִּי טֽוֹב”). Dual-cites: web:Ps.54.1 = oshb:Ps.54.3, web:Ps.54.6 = oshb:Ps.54.8. The two units coincide here (4 verses = 4 occurrences), so nothing is numerically wrong; the defect is that the reader cannot tell which was counted, and the suffixed and short forms in the same psalm — e.g. the divine title at oshb:Ps.54.6 beside אֱ֭לֹהִים — are precisely what the object-naming rule exists to exclude. Cure is one clause: name the spelling and the unit.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 55:1-8 = MT 55:2-9 (+1 psalm), title dual-cited correctly. The device_notes title description checks out against the bytes: MT 55:1 is “לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ בִּנְגִינֹ֗ת מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִֽד”, carrying the lamnatseach, maskil and le-David labels with no historical note, matching WEB's “For the Chief Musician. On stringed instruments. A contemplation by David.” (web:Ps.55.0). Selah verifies at MT 55:8 = web:Ps.55.7, one occurrence, and here it genuinely is verse-final in both witnesses. The back seam is strong and does not depend on the ground I contest: MT 55:10 opens “בַּלַּ֣ע אֲ֭דֹנָי”, a fresh imperative addressed against the city, breaking off the first-person flight-wish of MT 55:7-9 — that alone carries the 55:8|55:9 boundary, so the span stands and high confidence is defensible. The defect is in the rejected_alternative, which rejects the rival seam at 55:7 by asserting a continuity of quoted speech that the WEB rendering it invokes does not have.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative rests on the wish ‘continuing the same quoted speech into web:Ps.55.8’, but WEB closes its quotation at the end of 55:7 and opens a separate, self-contained quotation at 55:8.
challenges.evidence: WEB 55:6 opens the speech: “I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.” (web:Ps.55.6). WEB 55:7 closes it before the selah: “Behold, then I would wander far off. I would lodge in the wilderness.” Selah.” (web:Ps.55.7). WEB 55:8 then both opens and closes a new quotation: ““I would hurry to a shelter from the stormy wind and storm.”” (web:Ps.55.8). So in the witness the row cites, the quoted wish does not run continuously through 55:8. The MT gives no closing marker either way — MT 55:7 opens “וָאֹמַ֗ר” and nothing in MT 55:8-9 re-opens or terminates the speech (dual-cites: web:Ps.55.6 = oshb:Ps.55.7, web:Ps.55.8 = oshb:Ps.55.9) — so the substantive reading survives, but it has to be argued from the Hebrew's absent terminus, not from a WEB continuity that is not there. Span and seam are not contested.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 55:9-15 = MT 55:10-16. Every WEB string in the row is verbatim, and the two seams are sound: the front seam turns on the imperative “בַּלַּ֣ע אֲ֭דֹנָי” at MT 55:10, and the internal pivot the row uses to reject a 55:11|55:12 seam is byte-confirmed — MT 55:13 opens “כִּ֤י לֹֽא אוֹיֵ֥ב”, so the causal particle really does bind the betrayer's naming to the city description rather than separating them. Medium confidence is calibrated. The row also correctly avoids leaning on selah, which the inventory places nowhere in this span. The defect is a disclosure omission that this lens is specifically charged with: the verse the row quotes twice for its closing imprecation is a ketiv/qere verse, and the reading the imprecation depends on is the qere. The seam and the span are unaffected, which is why this is medium and not high.

challenges.claim: The row quotes web:Ps.55.15 twice for its closing imprecation, but that verse is MT 55:16, one of the book's ketiv/qere verses, and the row carries no K/Q disclosure even though the imprecation's force rests on the qere reading.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json records a ketiv/qere note at Ps.55.16 (MT-keyed; 68 notes over 65 verses book-wide). The bytes show it directly — MT 55:16 opens with the unpointed ketiv followed by the pointed qere: “ישימות יַשִּׁ֤י מָ֨וֶת”, full verse byte-spliced “ישימות יַשִּׁ֤י מָ֨וֶת עָלֵ֗ימוֹ יֵרְד֣וּ שְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים כִּֽי רָע֖וֹת בִּמְגוּרָ֣ם בְּקִרְבָּֽם”. WEB follows the qere: “Let death come suddenly on them.” (web:Ps.55.15), which is the very clause the row quotes as its imprecation, and the row's second quote “go down alive into Sheol.[fn 55:15 Sheol is the place of the dead.] For wickedness is among them, in their dwelling.” (web:Ps.55.15) comes from the same verse. Dual-cite: web:Ps.55.15 = oshb:Ps.55.16. Disclosure is owed because the verse is quoted, and it is single-witness; selecting a reading is not being asked for.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 55:16-19 = MT 55:17-20. The front seam is the strongest in this psalm's interior and I do not contest it: MT 55:17 opens “אֲ֭נִי אֶל אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֶקְרָ֑א”, a contrastive independent 1cs pronoun fronted before the verb, which is exactly what WEB's ‘As for me’ renders. The ordinal is also right — the inventory gives Psalm 55 exactly two selah verses, MT 55:8 and MT 55:20 (= web:Ps.55.7 and web:Ps.55.19), so ‘the psalm's second Selah’ is correct and the dual-cite arithmetic on it is correct. What is wrong is what the selah is said to do. In both witnesses the selah at this verse is verse-interior, and the verdict on the unrepentant that the row says it closes comes after it. The row's evidence base is thin enough for this to matter: boundary_evidence_refs holds two entries, one of which is this selah. A second, smaller defect: the rejected_alternative argues from web:Ps.55.20, outside the span, without mirroring it into the refs. The seam itself survives on the contrastive pronoun at the front and the referent narrowing at the back, so neither item is high, but medium confidence is if anything generous given the state of the back-seam warrant.

challenges.claim: The row has the second Selah ‘closing’ the strophe and the verdict on the unrepentant at web:Ps.55.19, but in both witnesses that selah is verse-interior and the verdict clause follows it rather than preceding it.
challenges.evidence: MT 55:20 byte-spliced in full: “יִשְׁמַ֤ע אֵ֨ל וְֽיַעֲנֵם֮ וְיֹ֤שֵׁ֥ב קֶ֗דֶם סֶ֥לָה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים” — the selah token סֶ֥לָה stands at token position 6 of 13, and the verdict clause “אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים” follows it to the end of the verse. WEB places it identically: “God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change and don’t fear God.” (web:Ps.55.19), where ‘Selah.’ is medial and the verdict sentence closes the verse. Dual-cite: web:Ps.55.19 = oshb:Ps.55.20. Contrast the same psalm's other selah, which is genuinely verse-final in both witnesses — MT 55:8 ends “אָלִ֖ין בַּמִּדְבָּ֣ר סֶֽלָה” and WEB 55:7 ends “I would lodge in the wilderness.” Selah.” (web:Ps.55.7) — so the distinction is available in this row's own psalm. As written the row credits the selah with marking a close it does not mark; the strophe's actual last words are the verdict, and the warrant should rest on the referent shift into MT 55:21 instead.

challenges.claim: web:Ps.55.20 is argued in the rejected_alternative but lies outside the span and does not appear in boundary_evidence_refs.
challenges.evidence: The span is Ps.55.16-Ps.55.19; the rejected_alternative turns on the referent of web:Ps.55.20 (“He raises his hands against his friends. He has violated his covenant.”, web:Ps.55.20 = oshb:Ps.55.21, MT “שָׁלַ֣ח יָ֭דָיו בִּשְׁלֹמָ֗יו חִלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתֽוֹ”, opening with the 3ms verb שָׁלַ֣ח). boundary_evidence_refs holds only web:Ps.55.16 and web:Ps.55.19 = oshb:Ps.55.20 (Selah), so the verse the alternative is decided on is not mirrored. The argument itself is correct — the plural referents of MT 55:20 do give way to a singular subject at MT 55:21 — which is why this is a mirroring defect rather than a substantive one.

reviews.reasoning: Span WEB 55:20-23 = MT 55:21-24, closing the psalm; the end of the span is the psalm's last verse and no row here crosses a psalm boundary. The referent shift the row rests on is byte-real: MT 55:21 opens “שָׁלַ֣ח יָ֭דָיו” with a singular subject, against the plural referents that close MT 55:20 (“לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים”), so the narrowing from plural to singular at the seam is correctly observed, and the out-of-span web:Ps.55.13 that the row reaches back to is properly mirrored in the refs. The closing WEB quote is verbatim and is genuinely the psalm's last verse. The defect is the same misdescription of the shared front-seam selah that the facing row carries: it is authored once and installed on both sides of the seam, so the cure is one edit applied to both. Medium confidence is calibrated.

challenges.claim: The row states that the front-seam Selah at web:Ps.55.19 closes the prior verdict, but the selah is verse-interior in both witnesses and the verdict clause follows it, so the front seam is not selah-marked in the way claimed.
challenges.evidence: MT 55:20 byte-spliced: “יִשְׁמַ֤ע אֵ֨ל וְֽיַעֲנֵם֮ וְיֹ֤שֵׁ֥ב קֶ֗דֶם סֶ֥לָה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים” — סֶ֥לָה is medial and is followed by “אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים”. WEB agrees: “God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change and don’t fear God.” (web:Ps.55.19). Dual-cite: web:Ps.55.19 = oshb:Ps.55.20. The seam at web:Ps.55.19|web:Ps.55.20 is not contested — it stands on the plural-to-singular referent shift into MT 55:21 (“שָׁלַ֣ח יָ֭דָיו בִּשְׁלֹמָ֗יו חִלֵּ֥ל בְּרִיתֽוֹ”), which is the row's other stated ground — but the selah cannot be described as closing the verdict when the verdict is what closes the verse. Because both rows meeting at this seam state it the same way, the repair belongs on both in one pass.
